captions: !Most games assume you can see well, reach, and hold a controller.
!Phengos: paper lights hide in your real room.
Catch them any way your body allows. Here: just look and hold for 1 s.
Caught. It pops, then flies to your palm.
Then it rises to your ceiling...
...and becomes the first star of tonight's constellation.
Point: a light peeks over the armchair. Depth occlusion hides the rest.
Aim the hand ray. Pinch.
Up it goes...
...and a line joins the new star to the last one.
Every catch becomes a star above the spot where that light hid.
Five catches later, the figure on your ceiling has grown.
Look (head): hold your view on a light; the ring fills in 1 s (0.5 to 2 s).
Quest 3 has no eye tracking, so this is head-gaze, and the game says so.
One switch: the outline steps through the lights, then Hint and Pause.
Any pinch, from either hand, catches what is outlined. One movement is enough.
Voice, optional: nine words, recognised on the device (Vosk). Nothing is sent.
Shown with a recorded test clip saying "catch next": one catch, one outline.
Pause opens every setting. Each one works by pointing, looking or one switch.
High contrast: the room redrawn as bold yellow outlines.
Text size up to 200%.
Big text, bold outlines, and the lights as solid yellow glows.
Sound only: the lights go dark. Each one hums from where it hides; pitch tells its height.
Every sound gets a caption with a direction. Hint pulses the nearest hum.
Meta VR Glasses profile: real eye gaze picks the light, a pinch catches it.
Here the mode reads Look (eyes). The black frame is the Glasses' field of view.
Leave and come back: your stars are still there, saved on this device.
!Phengos. Every way to play is a first-class way.
